description:
Context
- Retention controls v1 is adding tenant-configurable retention policies plus enforceable deletion/TTL across eligible datasets (audit logs first, then selected telemetry/analytics tables).
- Enterprise prospects have explicitly asked for legal hold semantics and an exception workflow that can be audited and demonstrated.

Goal
Implement a legal hold mechanism and retention exception flags that:
1) are represented in the control plane data model,
2) have clear authorization and audit logging requirements, and
3) are enforced by retention jobs (i.e., enforcement MUST respect holds/exceptions deterministically).

Non-goals (v1)
- “Matter management” (complex case objects, per-user holds, custodians).
- Full UI/UX and request intake workflow (tracked in Console/design + GRC process docs). This ticket provides backend primitives and enforcement semantics.

Definitions
- Legal hold: an override that prevents deletion/TTL enforcement for specific datasets and/or tenant environments, regardless of the configured retention policy.
- Retention exception: a time-bounded override that modifies retention for a dataset (typically extension of retention, sometimes immediate purge request is handled out-of-band). Exceptions must be attributable to a request and approver, and should have an expiration.

Proposed data model (control plane)
A. retention_holds
- id (uuid)
- tenant_id
- scope (enum): tenant | dataset
- dataset_type (nullable; required if scope=dataset) e.g., audit_logs, admin_activity, request_metadata, telemetry_eligible
- environment_scope (enum): all | hosted | dedicated | private (note: private may be “reported only” depending on deployment)
- region_scope (enum): all | <region>
- status (enum): active | released
- reason (text)
- request_id (text; optional link to GRC ticket)
- created_by (user_id/service)
- released_by (user_id/service; nullable)
- created_at, updated_at, released_at (nullable)

B. retention_exceptions
- id (uuid)
- tenant_id
- dataset_type
- environment_scope
- region_scope
- exception_type (enum): extend_retention | shorten_retention
- retention_days_override (int)
- effective_from (timestamp)
- expires_at (timestamp)  [required for v1; exceptions cannot be indefinite]
- reason (text)
- request_id (text)
- approved_by (user_id)
- created_by (user_id/service)
- created_at, updated_at

C. audit events
Every create/update/release action for holds and exceptions must generate an admin/audit event with:
- actor
- tenant_id
- action (create_hold, release_hold, create_exception, update_exception, revoke_exception)
- before/after snapshots (redacted as needed)
- request_id / correlation id

Policy evaluation semantics (effective policy computation)
- Effective retention policy for enforcement is:
  1) Start with computed retention policy per ENG-2912 (org/tenant/env precedence + guardrails).
  2) Apply retention_exceptions if active (effective_from <= now < expires_at) at the matching dataset/env/region scope.
  3) If any applicable retention_hold is active for the same scope, enforcement MUST treat retention as “infinite/blocked” for deletion purposes.
- Determinism requirement: given a timestamp and inputs (policy + holds + exceptions), effective policy output must be stable and testable (golden tests).

Enforcement requirements (audit log worker + eligible TTL)
- Enforcement workers (ENG-2920 audit logs; ENG-2921 telemetry TTLs where applicable) must call a shared library/service to fetch the effective enforcement directive:
  - {allowed: true/false, retention_days: int, reason_code: policy|exception|hold, hold_id/exception_id if applicable}
- When allowed=false due to hold:
  - job must skip deletion for the affected tenant/dataset scope
  - emit a metric with labels (dataset_type, env, reason_code=hold)
  - write an enforcement run record that includes “skipped_due_to_hold=true” and the hold_id(s) for auditability
- When exception modifies retention:
  - enforcement uses retention_days_override
  - enforcement run record includes exception_id
- Backfill: for existing tenants without holds/exceptions, behavior must be unchanged.

Authorization rules (Console + API)
- Read holds/exceptions:
  - Tenant Admin (RBAC) can view holds/exceptions affecting their tenant (needed for transparency, “why is retention not deleting?”)
  - Redwood Internal (support/security) can view for troubleshooting
- Create/release holds:
  - Restricted to Redwood Internal roles only (Security Eng / GRC) for hosted & dedicated
  - For Private deployments: allow customer-admin creation only if the customer is operating their own control plane instance AND has a configured “Compliance Admin” role; otherwise, reported as not supported (align with product requirements)
- Create exceptions:
  - Redwood Internal only for hosted/dedicated v1
  - Must require approved_by to be populated (enforced server-side)
- All mutating actions require explicit reason + request_id (server-side validation)

API surface (control plane)
- GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention/holds
- POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention/holds
- POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention/holds/{hold_id}:release
- GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention/exceptions
- POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention/exceptions
- PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention/exceptions/{exception_id}
- POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention/exceptions/{exception_id}:revoke

Validation/guardrails
- Holds cannot be created with empty reason.
- Exceptions must have expires_at, and expires_at must be <= 365 days from creation in v1 (guardrail; aligns with “no indefinite exceptions” requirement from eng-security thread).
- shorten_retention exceptions must still respect global minimum retention guardrail unless explicitly approved by Security Eng (we can implement this as a separate permission check or disallow in v1; see Open questions).

Testing & auditability
- Unit tests:
  - policy evaluation with holds/exceptions precedence
  - authz matrix for each endpoint
  - validation rules (expires_at required, reason required)
- Integration tests (where possible):
  - enforcement worker skipping behavior when hold is active
  - enforcement run records include hold_id/exception_id
- Golden tests in policy evaluation library (similar style to ENG-2912)

Rollout plan
- Feature-flag: retention_holds_exceptions_enabled
- Phase 1: ship schema + read-only endpoints + internal admin tooling usage (no Console surface)
- Phase 2: enable enforcement integration for audit logs first; monitor “skipped_due_to_hold” metrics and ensure no customer-impact regressions

Open questions
1) Do we allow shorten_retention exception type in v1? Product expectation is mostly “extend retention” for enterprise contracts, and “shorten” can conflict with audit/evidence needs. Proposal: ship extend_retention only in v1; keep enum but block shorten_retention behind internal-only allowlist.
2) Region scoping: for hosted multi-region tenants, should holds apply per-region or global by default? Proposal: default to region_scope=all to avoid partial deletion.
3) Private: confirm whether customer-admin can create holds in customer-operated control plane instances (Fatima Noor to advise).

Acceptance criteria
- Control plane has persistence + endpoints for legal holds and exceptions, with server-side validation and RBAC.
- All writes emit admin/audit events.
- Effective policy computation respects hold/exception precedence deterministically.
- Audit log enforcement worker refuses to delete data covered by an active hold and records evidence (metrics + run record).
- Docs: endpoint behavior and semantics documented in the internal runbook (link from Confluence process page).

Implementation tasks
- [ ] Add DB migrations for retention_holds + retention_exceptions
- [ ] Implement service layer + validation
- [ ] Implement authz checks (RBAC roles + internal-only constraints)
- [ ] Emit audit events for all mutations
- [ ] Update policy evaluation library to incorporate holds/exceptions
- [ ] Update enforcement worker interface to consume effective enforcement directive
- [ ] Add tests (unit + golden)

Notes
- Coordinate with Olga Petrov / Daniel Carter on audit/event fields needed for compliance reporting pack evidence snapshots.
- Coordinate with Kevin Osei on export semantics: exports should disclose when holds prevent deletion (but still only export within retention boundaries when no hold is present).
comments: 2025-01-24 (Naomi Feldman): We need legal hold semantics to be extremely crisp for security questionnaires. Please ensure tenants can at least VIEW an active hold (they don’t need to create it), and we can point to an audit trail of who placed it and when.

2025-01-28 (Jordan Lee): For determinism, recommend computing an “effective enforcement directive” as a pure function over policy + holds + exceptions + now. Avoid sprinkling hold checks throughout workers.

2025-02-03 (Olga Petrov): For evidence, we’ll need (a) exportable list of holds/exceptions with request_id + approver, and (b) proof enforcement skipped deletions (run record + metric screenshots). Please include IDs in run records so we can trace.

2025-02-06 (Kevin Osei): Enforcement worker can add labels for hold/exception; make sure cardinality stays bounded (don’t label by tenant_id in metrics). Use hold_id/exception_id only in run record, not Prometheus labels.

2025-02-10 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Authz proposal: customer Tenant Admin can read holds/exceptions; only Redwood Internal can write for hosted/dedicated. For Private, we’ll gate write access behind a separate role that only exists in customer-managed control plane installs. Awaiting Fatima’s guidance.

2025-02-14 (Sean Gallagher): Please add a safety valve: if hold lookup fails (control plane outage), workers should fail closed (skip deletions) rather than delete. Emit an alertable error metric so SRE can investigate.

2025-02-18 (Marcus Lin): Aligning on v1 scope: ship extend_retention exceptions; shorten_retention will remain internal-only (explicit allowlist) until Legal signs off on contract language and we have clearer audit implications.
